    // The worst distance from a face's own vertices to that face's plane. Zero
    // to rounding for every solid in the catalog above; non-zero is exactly the
    // damage `ProjectedToUnitSphere` does to a face-transitive Catalan.
    FacePlanarityDeviation(self: PolygonMesh3D, face: Integer): Number
    {
        var normal = self.FaceUnitNormal(face);
        var centroid = self.FaceCentroid(face);
        return self.FacePositions(face)
            .Map(p => normal.Dot(centroid.Between(p)).Abs)
            .Reduce(0.0, (acc, d) => acc.Max(d));
    }

    // The worst face planarity deviation over the whole mesh.
    PlanarityDeviation(self: PolygonMesh3D): Number
        => self.FaceCount
            .MapRange(f => self.FacePlanarityDeviation(f))
            .Reduce(0.0, (acc, d) => acc.Max(d));

    // Sphericity: the surface area of a ball of the same volume, over the actual
    // surface area (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphericity). One for a ball and
    // below one for everything else, so it rises monotonically along a Conway
    // program that adds faces. Precondition: a closed, outward-wound mesh.
    Sphericity(self: PolygonMesh3D): Number
        => Number.Pi.Pow(1.0 / 3.0)
            * (6.0 * self.EnclosedVolume).Pow(2.0 / 3.0)
            / self.TotalFaceArea;

    // The Euler characteristic V - E + F: two for every closed surface of genus
    // zero, which every operator above preserves
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_characteristic).
    EulerCharacteristic(self: PolygonMesh3D): Integer
        => self.VertexCount - self.UndirectedEdgeCount + self.FaceCount;

    //==
    // # Polyhedral dual pairings on the solid kinds
    //
    // The known dual-polyhedron partner of each named solid kind, as total maps on
    // the kind sums in `solids.types.plato`
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dual_polyhedron). This is the identity-level
    // counterpart of the geometric Conway `Dual` on `PolygonMesh3D`
    //: that operation constructs the dual mesh of
    // any mesh; these maps record which named form the dual of a named form is, so
    // the Archimedean/Catalan pairing is vocabulary rather than a catalog comment.
    // Dual is an involution: `kind.Dual.Dual == kind` for every kind below.

    // The dual Platonic solid: cube and octahedron swap, dodecahedron and
    // icosahedron swap, and the tetrahedron is self-dual
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platonic_solid).
    Dual(self: PlatonicSolid): PlatonicSolid
        => match (self) {
            Tetrahedron => PlatonicSolid.Tetrahedron;
            Cube => PlatonicSolid.Octahedron;
            Octahedron => PlatonicSolid.Cube;
            Dodecahedron => PlatonicSolid.Icosahedron;
            Icosahedron => PlatonicSolid.Dodecahedron;
        };

    // The Catalan dual of each Archimedean solid
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalan_solid).
    Dual(self: ArchimedeanSolid): CatalanSolid
        => match (self) {
            TruncatedTetrahedron => CatalanSolid.TriakisTetrahedron;
            Cuboctahedron => CatalanSolid.RhombicDodecahedron;
            TruncatedCube => CatalanSolid.TriakisOctahedron;
            TruncatedOctahedron => CatalanSolid.TetrakisHexahedron;
            Rhombicuboctahedron => CatalanSolid.DeltoidalIcositetrahedron;
            TruncatedCuboctahedron => CatalanSolid.DisdyakisDodecahedron;
            SnubCube => CatalanSolid.PentagonalIcositetrahedron;
            Icosidodecahedron => CatalanSolid.RhombicTriacontahedron;
            TruncatedDodecahedron => CatalanSolid.TriakisIcosahedron;
            TruncatedIcosahedron => CatalanSolid.PentakisDodecahedron;
            Rhombicosidodecahedron => CatalanSolid.DeltoidalHexecontahedron;
            TruncatedIcosidodecahedron => CatalanSolid.DisdyakisTriacontahedron;
            SnubDodecahedron => CatalanSolid.PentagonalHexecontahedron;
        };

    // The Archimedean dual of each Catalan solid: the inverse of the map above
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archimedean_solid).
    Dual(self: CatalanSolid): ArchimedeanSolid
        => match (self) {
            TriakisTetrahedron => ArchimedeanSolid.TruncatedTetrahedron;
            RhombicDodecahedron => ArchimedeanSolid.Cuboctahedron;
            TriakisOctahedron => ArchimedeanSolid.TruncatedCube;
            TetrakisHexahedron => ArchimedeanSolid.TruncatedOctahedron;
            DeltoidalIcositetrahedron => ArchimedeanSolid.Rhombicuboctahedron;
            DisdyakisDodecahedron => ArchimedeanSolid.TruncatedCuboctahedron;
            PentagonalIcositetrahedron => ArchimedeanSolid.SnubCube;
            RhombicTriacontahedron => ArchimedeanSolid.Icosidodecahedron;
            TriakisIcosahedron => ArchimedeanSolid.TruncatedDodecahedron;
            PentakisDodecahedron => ArchimedeanSolid.TruncatedIcosahedron;
            DeltoidalHexecontahedron => ArchimedeanSolid.Rhombicosidodecahedron;
            DisdyakisTriacontahedron => ArchimedeanSolid.TruncatedIcosidodecahedron;
            PentagonalHexecontahedron => ArchimedeanSolid.SnubDodecahedron;
        };

    //==
    // # The five Platonic solids as polygon meshes
    //
    // The regular convex polyhedra (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platonic_solid),
    // each as an explicit vertex table and face table, centred on the origin and
    // projected onto the unit sphere so the circumscribed radius is one. Read as
    // `PolygonMesh3D.Cube`, `PolygonMesh3D.Icosahedron`, … (the constant idiom:
    // dispatch on an ignored receiver of the result type).
    //
    // These five are the SEEDS: every other catalog solid in this tree is a Conway
    // program over one of them rather than
    // another table. Faces wind counter-clockwise seen from outside
    // (Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Winding, handedness, and normals).
    //
    // The tables are literal because the vertex coordinates ARE the definition —
    // golden-ratio rectangles for the icosahedron, a cube plus golden rectangles
    // for the dodecahedron. Generating them from symmetry groups instead would
    // hide, not explain. C# oracle: `Ara3D.Geometry.Polyhedra`.

    // Four triangles, four vertices: alternate corners of a cube
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrahedron).
    Tetrahedron(_: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
    {
        var h = 1.0 / Number.SqrtTwo;
        var points = [Point3D(1.0, 0.0, -h),
                      Point3D(-1.0, 0.0, -h),
                      Point3D(0.0, 1.0, h),
                      Point3D(0.0, -1.0, h)];
        var faces = [[0, 1, 2], [1, 0, 3], [0, 2, 3], [1, 3, 2]];
        return PolygonMeshOfVertexNumbers(points, faces).ProjectedToUnitSphere;
    }

    // Six squares, eight vertices (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cube).
    Cube(_: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
    {
        var points = [Point3D(-1.0, -1.0, -1.0),
                      Point3D(-1.0, 1.0, -1.0),
                      Point3D(1.0, 1.0, -1.0),
                      Point3D(1.0, -1.0, -1.0),
                      Point3D(-1.0, -1.0, 1.0),
                      Point3D(-1.0, 1.0, 1.0),
                      Point3D(1.0, 1.0, 1.0),
                      Point3D(1.0, -1.0, 1.0)];
        var faces = [[0, 1, 2, 3], [1, 5, 6, 2], [7, 6, 5, 4],
                     [4, 0, 3, 7], [4, 5, 1, 0], [3, 2, 6, 7]];
        return PolygonMeshOfVertexNumbers(points, faces).ProjectedToUnitSphere;
    }

    // Eight triangles on the six axis points: the dual of the cube
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octahedron).
    Octahedron(_: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
    {
        var points = [Point3D(1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
                      Point3D(-1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
                      Point3D(0.0, 1.0, 0.0),
                      Point3D(0.0, -1.0, 0.0),
                      Point3D(0.0, 0.0, 1.0),
                      Point3D(0.0, 0.0, -1.0)];
        var faces = [[0, 2, 4], [0, 4, 3], [0, 3, 5], [0, 5, 2],
                     [1, 2, 5], [1, 5, 3], [1, 3, 4], [1, 4, 2]];
        return PolygonMeshOfVertexNumbers(points, faces).ProjectedToUnitSphere;
    }
